searchText: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/v1.0.0-alpha.9/src/engine/authentication.md#key-distribution seems inconsistent about whether JWT keys can be > 256 bits: > The EL and CL clients MUST accept a cli/config parameter: jwt-secret, which designates a file containing the hex-encoded 256 bit secret key to be used for verifying/generating jwt tokens. > > ... > > If such a parameter is given, but the file cannot be read, or does not contain a hex-encoded key of at least 256 bits, the client should treat this as an error: either abort the startup, or show error and continue without exposing the authenticated port. would a >256-bit JWT key be spec-compliant? cc <@211091239112671234> Regardless of what people think here, the spec should be clearer on this point -- either "at least" or not "at least" but not both Geth only allows secrets of exactly 32 byte, so we should change the second sentence imo My preference as well. Theoretical, not-that-useful flexibility that's not well-tested is a liability <dannyryan> My preference as well, especially considering I'm almost certain their is no compelling reason for longer keys Also my preference https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/242 <dannyryan> approved. will leave it up for review for at least 24 hours. thanks!

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content:
https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/v1.0.0-alpha.9/src/engine/authentication.md#key-distribution seems inconsistent about whether JWT keys can be > 256 bits:
> The EL and CL clients MUST accept a cli/config parameter: jwt-secret, which designates a file containing the hex-encoded 256 bit secret key to be used for verifying/generating jwt tokens.
> 
> ...
> 
> If such a parameter is given, but the file cannot be read, or does not contain a hex-encoded key of at least 256 bits, the client should treat this as an error: either abort the startup, or show error and continue without exposing the authenticated port.

would a >256-bit JWT key be spec-compliant?

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: Regardless of what people think here, the spec should be clearer on this point -- either "at least" or not "at least" but not both

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Geth only allows secrets of exactly 32 byte, so we should change the second sentence imo

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: My preference as well. Theoretical, not-that-useful flexibility that's not well-tested is a liability

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> My preference as well, especially considering I'm almost certain their is no compelling reason for longer keys
